title: open-stream-derefs-freed-volatile-url-wrapper-hash-at-request-shutdown-uaf (CWE-416 use-after-free) in main/streams/streams.c
live_proof: measured at the pin, not inferred: on a build of php-5.0.0 from the museum tarball (sha256-pinned by the source corpus's src/) the trigger reports ASAN:heap-use-after-free with the detector patches, and ASAN:heap-use-after-free with Zend's allocator as shipped (results/20261028-host-asan/matrix.tsv, run 2026-10-28). The defective construct is in the pin's own source at main/streams/streams.c:1403, quoted in PROVENANCE.md. Upstream fixed it in d5bb03b11a96, the commit the source corpus records; php-src's history is not available on this host, so the fix hunk is cited by hash and not quoted
fidelity: the trigger is the source corpus's own script for this defect, carried over byte for byte from its corpus/CRASH-072.php; it is upstream-report-derived rather than a reduction of ours, and it drives the defect through the CLI SAPI on the whole interpreter, so it does not isolate the defective construct from the rest of the request. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it

host-asan.oracle: the report ASan produces on a build of the pin with the source corpus's two detector patches (Zend's size-class cache off, REAL_SIZE unrounded): heap-use-after-free, first frame _php_stream_free (main/streams/streams.c:350)

allocator_layer: the system allocator: the block's release reaches libc -- free(), called directly -- so musl mallocng (virtual profile) and CheriBSD's malloc both see the lifetime end
nested_why: the object comes straight from libc: zend_strndup (zend_alloc.c:413) for CRASH-068, a persistent hash table (zend_hash_init(..., persistent=1)) for CRASH-072, and each is released by a bare free()
layer_note: with Zend's allocator as shipped the host reading is ASAN:heap-use-after-free, against ASAN:heap-use-after-free with the cache disabled -- which is what places this case in the system-allocator corpus
